action: Check Point advises installing the November Jumbo Hotfix on all Management Servers and Security Gateways, starting with internet-facing Mobile Access deployments. Hunt for the published indicators and ask Check Point Support for an exposure assessment.
date_note: Day Check Point published its advisory and research; the exploitation it describes began on 30 October.

evidence.quote: Only a couple of dozen unpatched systems, in a single region, were compromised in the observed incidents.

exec: A fix existed a week before the attacks; only unpatched gateways were hit, and a small number in one region were wiped.
plain: Check Point says attackers broke into a couple of dozen of its security devices that lacked a fix issued on October 23. Some Israeli organisations had data wiped; later attacks in other countries were not destructive.

key_findings: Attackers used PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, CVSS 9.2) in the Mobile Access Portal for unauthenticated code execution, then CVE-2026-123039 to become root.
Exploitation began October 30, about a week after the PHP2Shell hotfix of October 23; the advisory counts a couple of dozen compromised unpatched systems.
The first wave targeted Israeli organisations and was destructive in a limited number of cases; a second wave from November 2 reached organisations in several countries with no destruction reported.
Tools included the TSGA backdoor, a TSProxy library, PHP webshells, a network scanner and a wiper that was also run on a VMware ESXi host reached over SSH.
Check Point Research links the tooling to the PhiliKit framework but does not attribute the campaign with confidence and raises a possible false flag.
report.publisher: Check Point (security advisory and Check Point Research)
recommendations: Install the November Jumbo Hotfix on all Management Servers and Security Gateways as soon as possible.
Hunt for the published indicators, including a process masquerading as a Check Point daemon and unexplained gaps in firewall logs.
Contact Check Point Support for exposure assessment; absence of an indicator match does not rule out compromise.

summary: Check Point says attackers chained the PHP2Shell flaws in the Mobile Access Portal with a Gaia privilege escalation to gain root on unpatched gateways from October 30, a week after a fix on October 23. A first wave hit Israeli organisations, destructive in some cases; a second wave from November 2 reached several countries without destruction. Check Point says only a couple of dozen unpatched systems were compromised.
title: Unpatched Check Point gateways wiped in PHP2Shell attacks

validation.note: Check Point (advisory and Check Point Research report) and Security Affairs each state the chain, the Oct 30 and Nov 2 waves, the Israeli wiper wave and a couple of dozen compromised systems; BleepingComputer and CSO Online (13 Nov) quote the same Check Point count. No confident attribution: Check Point Research cannot assess the operation with high confidence.
